evals.name: cut-next-beta
evals.prompt: let's cut the next beta of the python sdk and get it up on pypi
evals.expected_output: Runs preflight; notices current 0.1.0b1 is NOT on PyPI so the target is finishing 0.1.0b1 (re-tag) rather than bumping to b2; drafts CHANGELOG from the diff; stops at the push gate without publishing.
assertions: Runs the preflight checks (branch is main, clean tree, in sync with origin, CI green on HEAD, CHANGELOG has an Unreleased section)
Checks whether the current version 0.1.0b1 is already on PyPI before deciding the target
Given 0.1.0b1 is unpublished, targets finishing 0.1.0b1 (re-release) rather than proposing a bump to 0.1.0b2
Drafts CHANGELOG entries from git log since the last tag, grouped by Conventional Commit type
Reaches the tag-push gate and stops for explicit confirmation; does not push
Does not execute git push or publish anything

evals.name: recover-build-failure
evals.prompt: the release-python run for 0.1.0b2 died during the wheel build step. what should i do?
evals.expected_output: Explains a build failure means the publish job was skipped, so 0.1.0b2 is still free; recommends fixing the bug in repo files and re-tagging the SAME version at the fixed commit; does not recommend bumping.
assertions: Recognizes that a build failure means the publish job was skipped, so the version is still free
Recommends re-tagging the SAME version (0.1.0b2), not bumping to a new version
Includes the caveat that the re-tag must point at the fixed commit (tag-triggered workflow uses the workflow file at the tagged commit)
Does not recommend bumping to a new version number

evals.name: publish-final-version
evals.prompt: i think we're ready to publish wardex-sdk 0.1.0 — the real one, out of beta
evals.expected_output: Honors the explicit 0.1.0 target; runs preflight incl. PyPI check for 0.1.0; drafts changelog; notes 0.1.0 is a final (installed by pip by default, unlike betas); stops at the gate.
assertions: Runs preflight including a PyPI check for the 0.1.0 target
Honors the user's explicit 0.1.0 target instead of overriding it with a different version
Notes that 0.1.0 is a final release (pip installs it by default, unlike a pre-release)
Reaches the push gate and stops without publishing
